how: a git stash pop onto a branch lacking the intervening commit conflicted. A later git add -A swept the conflicted file in

summary: stage 3 is INERT: PostToolUse never fires on a failing command, so no failure is ever recorded
measured: probe2, one repo, two sole-command runs against the installed 0.4.0 plugin. python3 test_always_fails.py exit 1 created NOTHING - no .claude directory at all. python3 test_always_passes.py exit 0 created .claude and a four-field stamp. Same repo, same cwd, same command shape
the_script_is_fine: feeding the installed post-bash.sh a synthetic payload with exitCode 1 writes the ledger correctly. The hook is never invoked, so flake_record is never reached
consequence: post-bash cannot observe a failure, the ledger is never written by the real harness, and a re-run pass is indistinguishable from a first pass. That is precisely the hole stage 3 exists to close. The mechanism is merged, public, documented as shipped, and cannot fire
the_contradiction: stage 1's inferred stamp is SAFE because PostToolUse does not fire for a non-zero exit - that premise is stated in this repository's own README. Stage 3 requires the OPPOSITE. Two mechanisms in one kit with mutually exclusive premises, and the conflict was written down before stage 3 was designed
why_the_controls_missed_it: every control feeds a synthetic payload carrying an exitCode, because that is what the design assumed the harness sends. The suites test the script against the payload it was written for, never against the payload the harness actually delivers - which is none
possible_fix_unverified: PreToolUse fires on every Bash call. Recording 'command started' there and 'command completed' in PostToolUse would make a started-but-never-completed test command detectable as a failure. NOT tested, and interrupted calls and session crashes would need handling

summary: STAGE 1 FAIL-OPEN: a failing test run does not clear the stamp, and the commit is allowed
proven_end_to_end: in one repo against the installed 0.4.0 plugin: python3 test_always_passes.py exit 0 wrote the stamp; python3 test_always_fails.py exit 1 left it untouched; the commit was ALLOWED and produced 913d2f9
root_cause: the same discovery as INC-0024. post-bash.sh:501 prints 'Tests/build FAILED or unreadable. Stamp cleared.' and that branch is DEAD CODE in the real harness, because PostToolUse does not fire for a failing Bash call. Failure handling was written, tested against synthetic payloads, and never runs
realistic_shape: it does not need the same command twice. npm test passes and stamps; npm run test:integration fails and clears nothing; the commit goes through on the first suite's stamp while the second is red
why_it_is_worse_than_INC_0024: stage 3 being inert means a mechanism does not help. This means the flagship mechanism PERMITS a commit after a failing test run. Stage 1 is rated keep, is shipped, is public, and is the thing the whole kit is named for
mitigations_real_but_partial: any file EDIT still clears the stamp, and the stamp expires after 30 minutes, so the window is a passing run followed by a failing run with no edit between. That is an ordinary sequence, not a contrived one
the_fix_is_the_same_one: a PostToolUseFailure hook. The harness UI states its payload carries tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, error, error_type, is_interrupt and is_timeout - enough to clear the stamp on a real failure while ignoring interrupts and timeouts

summary: evidence-required completion: fix — the stamp survives a failing test run
why: proven end to end: a passing run stamped, a failing run left the stamp untouched, and the commit was permitted. post-bash.sh:501 clears the stamp on failure and that branch has never executed, because PostToolUse does not fire for a failing Bash call
what_keep_was_based_on: stage 1's addendum 2 observed the hooks firing from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, a refusal, and a release. All true and still true. No probe ever ran a FAILING test command and then attempted a commit
the_lesson: a mechanism's happy path and its refusal path are not its whole behaviour. The third path - what happens when the thing being verified FAILS - was written in the code and never exercised against the harness
to_close: a live session where a failing run clears the stamp and the following commit is refused

summary: PR #12 PostToolUseFailure hook: fix — Codex found 3 High, two verified by reproduction
reviewers: Codex 0.153.2, single round, primed with the one defect I had already found
high_1_verified: RUN_LEAD is both too narrow and too wide. Reproduced: 'bash -x test-hooks.sh' and 'python3 -u test_x.py' do NOT match, so real runs would not clear; 'pytest-other' and 'npm testing' DO match, because the runner alternatives carry no token boundary. The same weakness exists in shipped stamping today
high_3_verified: wrong-repository clearing. stamp_target_dir_from_command takes the FIRST textual cd. Reproduced: 'npm test; cd /repo-B; false' resolves to /repo-B, and 'cd /repo-A && cd /repo-B && npm test' resolves to /repo-A. Both clear an innocent repo and leave the red one stamped. Only reachable because I accept chained commands; post-bash refuses them
high_7: a missing classifier makes post-bash refuse to stamp, which is safe, but makes post-bash-failure refuse to clear, which reopens INC-0025. The two callers need opposite fallbacks
my_own_control_passed_for_the_wrong_reas: control 6 asserts a chained command clears the stamp, using 'cd /tmp && npm test'. The resolver returns /tmp, which is not a repository, so it fell back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and cleared the seeded repo by accident rather than by the behaviour claimed. Seventh instance of this defect class, written into the same PR whose message boasts about catching it
section_9_is_theatre: the control section titled 'the payload contract this hook depends on' manufactures the same payload every time, so it cannot detect a real payload that disagrees - which is the exact thing it was written to catch
also: malformed JSON exits silently rather than announcing; liberal CLEARING was wrongly extended to liberal FLAKE RECORDING, so 'cd /missing && npm test' records a flake though no test ran; 'npm test || true' hides a red suite from the event entirely; is_timeout is in the harness UI but not the published docs

summary: the local controls refuted the cross-vendor review's suggested fix, and were right
what_happened: Codex correctly observed that RUN_LEAD does not match 'bash -x test-hooks.sh' or 'python3 -u test_x.py', which are real runs — fail-closed for stamping, FAIL-OPEN for clearing. I verified it and applied the suggested fix, a flag group after each wrapper. EIGHTEEN controls in test-post-bash.sh went red at once
why_the_fix_was_wrong: some flags mean DO NOT ACTUALLY RUN — bash -n, ruby -c, perl -c, node -e, command -v — so admitting them writes a GREEN stamp for a command that executed no suite. That is a false pass, strictly worse than the fail-open it fixes. Others consume the next token, sudo -u and bash -O, so the apparent suite is a flag's argument
the_controls_were_written_to_stop_exactl: their names carry '(flag class deleted)'. Someone had already tried this fix and written controls against its return. They worked, on a reviewer who had not read them and on me
the_pattern_worth_keeping: an external reviewer sees what local controls encode as assumption; local controls remember what an external reviewer cannot know. Neither is sufficient. The observation was right and the prescription was wrong, and only running the suite could tell those apart
outcome: reverted, and the reasoning written into classify-test-commands.sh so the next person does not spend the same hour. The limitation is now stated in the README in both directions: a wrapped-with-flags run neither stamps nor clears

summary: post-bash resolves the stamp directory from arbitrary command text, and can target the wrong repo
two_paths: both reproduced against the shipped resolver. MASKED CHAIN: post-bash.sh:222 strips the prefix with sed 's/^cd [^&]*&&//', and [^&]* spans a semicolon, so 'cd /repo-A; cd /repo-B && npm test' normalises to a clean 'npm test'. ARGUMENT TEXT: stamp_target_dir_from_command SEARCHES for a cd, so 'npm test -- --grep "please cd /repo-B now"' resolves to /repo-B
consequence_for_stamping: a passing suite in repository A can write its stamp into repository B, unlocking a commit in a repository nothing tested, while A stays locked. Fail-open and fail-closed at once, which is the same shape as the 2026-08-10 shared-stamp defect
not_fixed_here: post-bash-failure.sh parses the prefix strictly and never hands the resolver a raw command line, so the new hook is clean. post-bash.sh is UNCHANGED - it has 168 controls encoding its current behaviour and changing it needs its own controls and its own change
severity_reasoning: medium rather than high because it needs a command that both names another repository and runs a suite, which is unusual, and because the wrong-direction failure locks rather than unlocks in the common case. It is still a stamp written somewhere nobody tested

summary: I broke 'npm run test:unit' while fixing 'pytest-other', and 168 controls said nothing
what: adding a trailing token boundary to the runner list stopped 'npm run test:unit', 'make test-all' and 'pytest>out.log' matching. The first is one of the most common test commands there is. Reverted within the hour
it_did_not_even_work: a quote was included in the boundary class, so 'pytest""-other' - which the shell concatenates back to pytest-other - still matched. The fix broke common commands and left the hole open
the_real_finding: none of the 168 controls in test-post-bash.sh runs 'npm run test:unit', so nothing caught a regression on the single most common form. A suite can be large, green, mutation-tested and still have no case for the thing everybody actually types
left_open: the pytest-other false positive stands, recorded in the library. It fires on a command nobody runs by accident; breaking one everybody runs costs more. The correct fix distinguishes a script-name suffix from an unrelated longer word, which needs per-alternative rules and its own controls

summary: evidence-required completion: keep — a failing run cleared the stamp in a live session
observed: plugin 0.5.1 installed; python3 test_passes.py wrote the stamp, python3 test_fails.py CLEARED it. First time a failing test command has cleared a stamp in this project
correction: REV-0013's addendum claimed hooks are fixed at session start and the fix could not be observed in the session that wrote it. False. /reload-plugins took the hook count 7 to 8 and the hook fired immediately. Only settings.json hooks do not reload

summary: flake recording was inert for the command shape agents actually produce
found_by: running it, not by controls. In a live session the stamp cleared correctly on every failing suite and the ledger was never written once
cause: a cd prefix excluded a failure from being RECORDED. That rule was added for a real reason - cd /missing && npm test fails before any suite runs, so recording it would make a later identical pass read as flaky and cost a declaration and a trailer. But cd /repo && npm test is how an agent almost always invokes a suite. Excluding all of them meant flake triage stayed inert for a second, quieter reason than INC-0024
why_no_control_caught_it: every control supplies the command shape its author imagined. Only running the thing produces the shape the harness makes. 37 controls, 10 mutants, and not one case with a cd prefix that mattered
fix: record when the cd could have SUCCEEDED, tested by whether the target directory exists. Keeps the original objection where it applies and restores recording for the common shape. Three controls added, four mutants killed
the_pattern: this is the third time in one day that a mechanism was correct against its controls and wrong against the harness. INC-0024, INC-0025, and now this

summary: I generalised one observation about settings.json hooks into a rule about all hooks
the_claim: that hooks are fixed at session start, so a fix could not be observed in the session that wrote it. It went into two trial records, the README and a plugin description
the_evidence_it_rested_on: a PostToolUseFailure probe added to ~/.claude/settings.json did not fire after being written mid-session. True, and it is still true
what_was_actually_the_case: /reload-plugins reloads PLUGIN hooks. It took the count from 7 to 8 and the new hook fired immediately in the same session. Only settings.json hooks needed a restart
cost: most of an afternoon spent believing a shipped fix was untestable, and four documents asserting it
the_habit: one observation about one mechanism became a rule about a category, and the rule was written into public documentation without being checked once

summary: keep now requires a live observation, and the trial template gains two required runs
decision: Serina, 2026-09-07, after three defects in one day were correct against 512 controls and wrong against the harness: running it becomes part of the process alongside review, not instead of it
the_sharpening: 'run the tests and see green' would have caught none of them - the suites were green throughout. What worked was running the MECHANISM in a live session and watching behaviour, especially when the thing being verified failed
run_1: a measurement spike BEFORE the design exists. Not 'does my thing work' but 'what does the harness actually send'. Would have caught INC-0024 before stage 3 was designed, in about twenty minutes, against a contradiction already written in the repository's own README
run_2: a live exercise BEFORE the pull request leaves draft, installing the worktree as a LOCAL marketplace - a directory is a valid marketplace source, so it never required merging first. Would have caught INC-0025 and INC-0027 without either shipping
template_changes: row 5 in the hostile-input table for the SUBJECT OF VERIFICATION failing; a required 'What was observed LIVE' section with both runs; a live table whose row 4 asks for the command shape an agent actually produces; and a verdict rule making keep unavailable without an observation
the_friction_is_recorded: a live run needs slash commands, so it needs a human, so an agent cannot do it alone. That friction is exactly why three stages shipped without one. The template says the rule is better deleted than left to be quoted if it becomes aspirational

summary: the evidence for the live-run rule: one run, two defects, neither findable by controls
the_run: 2026-09-06, plugin 0.5.1 installed, one repository, two commands. python3 test_passes.py then python3 test_fails.py
caught_1: INC-0025 CONFIRMED FIXED by observation - the stamp cleared. First time a failing test command had ever cleared a stamp in this project. That was the outstanding evidence two trial records had been blocked on for a day
caught_2: INC-0027 DISCOVERED by the same run - the stamp cleared every time and the flake ledger was never written once, because a cd prefix excluded recording and cd /repo && npm test is the shape agents actually produce. A defect nothing else had surfaced
why_no_control_could_have: every control supplies the command shape its author imagined; only running the thing produces the shape the harness makes. 37 controls and 10 mutants were green throughout
cost_of_the_run: about four minutes, three slash commands and two Bash calls
this_is_the_justification: CHG-0008 argues the rule from three defects. This is the direct measurement: one run, one confirmation and one discovery

summary: PR #12 round two: three more High, including two residual paths in my own fix
reviewers: Codex 0.153.2, second round, told what round one had produced so it would not re-find it
high_1: a MASKED CHAIN survived normalisation. Stripping the prefix with [^&]* also swallows a semicolon, so cd /repo-A; cd /repo-B && npm test became a clean npm test and the separator check never saw the chain. Reproduced
high_2: ARGUMENT TEXT steered the resolver. npm test -- --grep "please cd /repo-B now" resolved to /repo-B, so a failure in A would clear B and leave A verified. Reproduced
high_3: the token-boundary fix I had added unprompted in round one broke npm run test:unit, make test-all and pytest>out.log, and did not close its own hole because a quote was inside the boundary class. Reverted; NOTE-0022
also: a redirect can fail before the suite starts, so it should clear but not record; two remaining overclaims in hooks.json and the manifest
outcome: all closed in the same PR. 37 controls, 10 mutants killed. Codex confirmed the round-one flag-group rejection was correct and suggested a narrower per-wrapper form as future work

summary: main shipped a regression for about twenty minutes because a PR merged mid-repair
what: PR #12 was merged at ac1e892, one commit before the round-two review fixes landed. main therefore carried a broken token boundary - npm run test:unit and make test-all stopped matching, so neither earned a stamp - plus both wrong-repository paths
how_it_was_missed: the merge deleted the branch and my next push silently RE-CREATED it, reporting '[new branch]' rather than an update. Taking that at face value would have left main broken indefinitely; it was caught only by checking main after a merge I had not performed
direction_of_failure: fail-CLOSED for the regression - the suites refused to stamp rather than stamping wrongly - so no false green was possible in that window. The wrong-repo paths were the more serious half
fix: PR #13, merged. Verified against origin/main afterwards rather than assumed
lesson: verify main after a merge someone else performed, and read what a push actually reports

summary: CLOSED INC-0025: the stamp now clears on a failing run, observed in a live session
closed_by: post-bash-failure.sh on PostToolUseFailure, shipped in plugin 0.5.0 and refined through 0.5.2
the_observation: live session, plugin installed: python3 test_passes.py wrote the stamp, python3 test_fails.py CLEARED it. First time a failing test command has cleared a stamp in this project
time_to_resolution: about six and a half hours from discovery to observed fix, across four pull requests and two cross-vendor review rounds
what_it_cost_while_open: unknown but bounded - the defect existed for the life of the kit, and required a passing run followed by a failing run inside thirty minutes with no edit between. Any file edit cleared the stamp, which is why ordinary edit-test-commit work was unaffected
verdict_change: stage 1 keep -> fix -> keep. REV-0013 then REV-0015

summary: what keeps INC-0024 and INC-0027 open: the flaky path has never been watched end to end
state: both are fixed in code and green against 41 controls and 14 mutants. The recording half has been observed writing the ledger when the hook is invoked directly
what_has_NOT_been_seen: a full live sequence: a suite fails, the same suite then passes, the stamp reads flaky rather than clean, and a commit is refused naming the command and both times. Every link has been tested; the chain has not been run
why_that_matters_here: under the rule ruled today, keep requires a live observation, and this is precisely the observation missing. Closing them now would be the mistake this rule exists to prevent - three defects this week were correct against their controls and wrong against the harness
to_close: one live session: earn a stamp, fail a suite, pass the same suite, attempt a commit. Four Bash calls after a plugin update

summary: corrected: only INC-0024 is open on the flaky path; INC-0027 was already resolved
correction: NOTE-0025 said INC-0024 and INC-0027 were both open. INC-0027 was recorded with a resolved_ts when its fix landed, so it is closed. Superseded rather than edited, because an edited line is not evidence
what_is_actually_open: INC-0024 alone. It is fixed in code and green against 41 controls and 14 mutants, and the recording half has been observed writing the ledger when the hook is invoked directly
what_has_NOT_been_seen: a full live sequence - a suite fails, the same suite then passes, the stamp reads flaky rather than clean, and a commit is refused naming the command and both times. Every link has been tested; the chain has not been run
to_close: one live session: earn a stamp, fail a suite, pass the same suite, attempt a commit

summary: no defect in this record was found by one of the kit's own mechanisms
method: all 29 incidents classified by how they were FIRST noticed, from their own found_by fields plus commit messages and trial records. 5 excluded as closures or duplicates, 24 classified. Reconstructed 2026-09-07 and labelled as such - a judgement made today is not an observation made then, and events.jsonl is append-only so it lives in its own file rather than being retrofitted
the_result: running it 8, reading 8, adversarial review 6, mutation 1, a human asking a question 1, A MECHANISM FIRING 0
the_mechanisms_did_fire: repeatedly, and were right every time. What they caught were process slips - an undeclared test change, a suite missing from the runner, an unbumped version - recorded as NOTE-0013, NOTE-0014 and NOTE-0019. Not one defect
severity_split: two thirds of the high-severity defects came from running it. Eight of nine came from running or reviewing; the ninth from mutation. Reading found eight real defects and not one severe one
what_it_does_not_show: nothing about performance in other hands - one author, one machine, five days. And nothing about whether the mechanisms stop reward hacking, which is what they exist for. The single true positive in the programme was a version bump
my_own_table_was_wrong: the first draft of the severity matrix was hand-counted and wrong in five of fifteen cells. Recomputed from the record. Same defect this repository has already logged twice as a stale count printed with authority

summary: CLOSED INC-0024: the whole flake chain observed working in a live session
closed_by: post-bash-failure.sh on PostToolUseFailure, plugin 0.5.2, after INC-0027 fixed recording for the cd-prefixed command shape agents actually produce
the_observation: a genuinely flaky suite, one live session. Failing run wrote the ledger; the re-run pass stamped FLAKY not clean; the commit was REFUSED naming the command and both times - 'It failed at 07:59 and passed at 08:00, with no edit between'
both_printed_remedies_were_EXECUTED_not_: the declaration commands the gate printed were run verbatim, which produced a second correct refusal demanding the trailer; the trailer line it then printed was also run verbatim and allowed the commit. Git parsed the trailer and check-flaky-trailers read it back. This kit's ancestor shipped a refusal whose printed escape hatch was wrong, and the wrong route became the trained one
the_honest_path_still_costs_nothing: fail, EDIT a file, pass - stamp reads clean and the commit is allowed silently. No declaration, no trailer, no message. A mechanism that taxed ordinary debugging would be switched off
time_to_resolution: about thirty hours from discovery, across five pull requests, two cross-vendor review rounds and three plugin versions

summary: flake-triage hooks: keep — the whole chain observed, first verdict under the live-run rule
what_changed: fix -> keep. REV-0012 rated it fix because it had been observed live and did not work. It has now been observed live and does
false_positives_now_means_something: 0 measured against the honest-fix path in a live session, not against fixtures. Fail, edit, pass produced a clean stamp and a silent commit
true_positives_stays_0: the flake was a fixture written to be flaky. The mechanism refused exactly what it should have, and that is a demonstration rather than a defect caught
first_under_the_new_rule: CHG-0008 made keep conditional on a live observation, and that rule is what made this wait. The same evidence a day earlier would have been controls plus a scripted end-to-end - a combination that has now been wrong three times in this project
unchanged: command narrowing remains the headline limitation. This raises the cost of laundering a red suite; it does not prevent it

summary: post-bash-failure review: keep — all findings from both rounds closed
why_this_exists: REV-0014 and REV-0016 recorded the two cross-vendor review rounds on the hook, both with verdict fix. Every finding was closed, but neither was superseded - so a query over live verdicts still showed post-bash-failure as fix while the same component held keep under REV-0017. A report drawn from that list would have said stage 3 was unfinished
round_1_closed: wrong-repository clearing, naming-a-suite-is-not-running-one, and the missing-classifier fallback. All three fixed and controlled
round_2_closed: the masked chain surviving normalisation, argument text steering the resolver, and my own token-boundary change breaking npm run test:unit. All three fixed; the last reverted
deliberately_NOT_closed: INC-0026 - post-bash.sh shares the resolver defect and is untouched. It has 168 controls encoding current behaviour and needs its own change. Recorded rather than carried quietly
naming_note: this component appears under two mechanism names - post-bash-failure for the code reviews and flake-triage-hooks for the trial verdict. Same thing. A report should not count them twice

summary: post-bash-failure round one: superseded by REV-0018, all findings closed
why: supersedes takes ONE id, so REV-0018 could only close the round-two review. This closes round one, which was still showing a live fix verdict for a mechanism that holds keep
the_general_problem: a review chain has to be superseded link by link. Two rounds on one mechanism left two open verdicts, and only the second was obvious. Any future multi-round review needs the same walk, or a live-verdict query reports the earliest opinion rather than the latest

summary: deployed skills in ~/.claude/skills are 17 days stale: 5 differ, 27 never deployed
measured: 6 identical, 5 DIFFERENT, 27 on serina-learning main but absent from ~/.claude/skills
concrete_symptom: pr-gate.sh tells you verdict.sh resolves a test command from .superpowers/test-cmd or a Makefile test target; the DEPLOYED verdict.sh only reads VERDICT_TEST_CMD, so that instruction cannot be followed
same_shape_as: INC-0014 - a deployed copy drifting from source with nothing watching, silent until something needed it
not_broken_today: no skill is failing; the risk is instructions that reference behaviour the deployed copy lacks, and 27 skills sessions have never had
resolution_needed: human - refreshing 32 files under ~/.claude affects every concurrent session, so it is not a bulk copy to make unasked
recorded_late: observed 2026-09-05 but only appended to a working tree whose main was 48 commits stale; found uncommitted and re-recorded 2026-09-07. The stranded line claimed id INC-0016, which upstream had since assigned to a different incident - the collision INC-0020 warns about, reached by the same route
measurement_not_refreshed: the 17-day figure is as measured on 2026-09-05 and has not been re-run; treat it as a dated observation, not current state

summary: pr-gate instructs you to use verdict.sh options the deployed copy does not have
confirms: INC-0031's concrete_symptom, re-checked live at this event's ts — roughly 38 hours after the observation INC-0031 records
local_vs_utc: this was observed on the morning of 2026-09-07 New Zealand time, which is 2026-09-06 in UTC. The record stores UTC, so any morning-NZ event lands under the previous calendar day. INC-0031's recorded_late field says 're-recorded 2026-09-07' and means NZ local; it is not a contradiction of the UTC timestamps, and a report drawn from this file should state which clock it is quoting
how_surfaced: pr-gate.sh blocked 'gh pr create' on chore/record-skills-drift; its block message told the reader that verdict.sh resolves the test suite from VERDICT_TEST_CMD, .superpowers/test-cmd or a Makefile 'test:' target, and that --no-test-cmd waives it
verified: read ~/.claude/skills/review-final/verdict.sh directly: VERDICT_TEST_CMD is the only resolution present. No .superpowers/test-cmd, no Makefile target, no --no-test-cmd flag anywhere in the script
consequence: following the gate's own instructions literally fails — --no-test-cmd dies as an unknown argument, and the two extra resolution paths silently do not exist. The gate is correct to block; its remediation text is not
mechanism_did_not_catch: no control in the kit compares a hook's instructional text against the deployed script it names, so this was invisible until a human-facing block message was read closely
still_not_remeasured: only verdict.sh was re-checked. INC-0031's counts — 5 differing, 27 never deployed across 32 files — remain as measured on 2026-09-05 and have still not been re-run

summary: harness sends originalFile and a structuredPatch on every edit: diff-scoping needs no git
measured: 65 payloads captured live via a throwaway local-marketplace plugin, PreToolUse and PostToolUse for Bash, Edit and Write
edit_carries: tool_input.old_string and new_string on BOTH PreToolUse and PostToolUse; tool_response.originalFile is the complete prior file; tool_response.structuredPatch is a real diff hunk with oldStart, oldLines, newStart, newLines and lines
assumption_changed: that a diff-scoped mutation gate would have to shell out to git to reconstruct prior state. It does not - the harness hands over the patch and the original file synchronously, per edit
unplanned_option: old_string and new_string arrive on PreToolUse, so a weakening could be inspected BEFORE it reaches disk. Stronger than the advisory mechanism on the roadmap. Recorded as an option, not a decision
write_differs: Write gives originalFile null and an empty structuredPatch when CREATING a file, and both populated when overwriting. A gate assuming Write always carries prior state would break on every new file
gap_in_own_probe: the first Write created a new file, so overwrites were unmeasured until the hole was noticed and closed deliberately

summary: every hook payload carries cwd - the resolver INC-0026 needs was there all along
observed: cwd, session_id, prompt_id, transcript_path, permission_mode, effort.level, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input and tool_use_id are present on EVERY event captured, without exception
bearing_on_inc_0026: post-bash.sh resolves the stamp directory by parsing arbitrary command text, which is why a masked chain can target the wrong repository. The harness has been sending cwd in the payload the whole time
not_a_fix: this is a measurement, not a change. INC-0026 still needs its own work with its own controls, and 168 existing controls encode the current resolver's behaviour

summary: plugin cache served stale hook registrations after a version bump and a marketplace update
mechanism: local directory marketplace, throwaway stage4-spike plugin
observed: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT pointed at the marketplace SOURCE directory on all 65 captured events, so hook SCRIPTS ran live from source. But hooks.json REGISTRATIONS came from ~/.claude/plugins/cache, which still held version 0.0.1 with round-1 contents
what_was_done: plugin version bumped 0.0.1 to 0.0.2, then /plugin marketplace update, then /reload-plugins. No 0.0.2 directory was ever created in the cache
consequence: round 2 of the channel probe ran its NEW script under the OLD registration: no channel argument was passed, so the script minted nonces and emitted nothing on any channel. An instrument that looks alive and reports silence
relation_to_inc_0019: INC-0019 says the version must be bumped or the cache never copies. Here it WAS bumped and the cache still did not copy, so a version bump is necessary and not sufficient
why_it_matters: any live trial that edits hooks.json can silently exercise the old wiring while believing it tests the new. That invalidates the trial without failing anything
workaround: scripts are live, so moving probe logic into a script already registered on the wanted events reaches them with no reload and nothing asked of a human

summary: three attempts to measure which hook channel reaches a human, all three invalid
still_open: whether ANY hook output channel is DISPLAYED to a human. INC-0013 and INC-0016 remain open; this spike did not close them
attempt_1_leading_question: the agent named the exact string to look for and then asked whether it had been seen. Both yes answers confirm a supplied string rather than report a received one, so neither is evidence
attempt_2_silent_instrument: the script emitted nothing because the stale registration passed no channel argument, while still logging that it had. Only the nonce log distinguished no-output from no-hook; without that control the silence would have been recorded as a finding, which is the shape of INC-0018
attempt_3_own_control_killed_it: a transcript membership test returned YES for round-2 tokens that were never emitted on any channel, because the agent had printed the nonce log into a tool result itself
what_IS_established: structurally, hook output on all three channels on both PreToolUse and PostToolUse is recorded in the transcript as type=attachment records - channels A and B under attachment.stdout and attachment.content, channel C under attachment.stderr. Channel A's JSON systemMessage landed as raw stdout rather than a surfaced message
the_distinction: present in the transcript is not the same as shown to a human, and for an advisory mechanism the second is the only one that counts
method_for_next_attempt: fire a token the agent never logs, prints or reads beforehand, then ask the human to type back any hex they see. The agent cannot bias what it has not seen

summary: systemMessage reaches the user on PreToolUse and PostToolUse; stdout and stderr do not
answers: INC-0013's open research question - whether PreToolUse honours systemMessage. It does. So does PostToolUse, which is the half INC-0016 needs
method: six nonces emitted in one round, three channels across PreToolUse and PostToolUse. The agent did not read, print or know any token before Serina reported. The only route from hook to human was the channel itself
result: Serina reported exactly two of the six, and both were channel a - systemMessage - one per event. Plain stdout and stderr were emitted on both events and neither was seen
why_this_round_counts: the selectivity is the evidence. Two of six, both the same channel, from a set the reporter could not see in advance. The three earlier attempts failed on a leading question, an instrument that emitted nothing, and a transcript test its own control refuted - NOTE-0031
surfacing_format: the message arrives attributed to its origin, rendered as 'PreToolUse:Bash says: <text>'
confirms_prior_research: research/claude-code-hook-output-channels.md, written 2026-09-04 from documentation, said plain stdout and stderr at exit 0 reach the debug log and never the transcript. Observation agrees. The note's one open question is now closed by measurement rather than by reading
corrects_an_earlier_inference: this session earlier read channel a landing in attachment.stdout as evidence the JSON form was not honoured. That inference was wrong: it is recorded as stdout AND surfaced. Presence in the transcript says nothing either way about display, which was the distinction being argued at the time and then not applied to the reading
consequence_for_stage_4: mutation-gate can ship advisory and be read. The roadmap entry survives its first design risk
consequence_for_the_two_incidents: INC-0013 and INC-0016 stay OPEN because nothing is fixed yet, but they stop being research. guard-test-changes.sh, verify-gate.sh and post-bash.sh announce on stdout or stderr - the two channels that reach nobody - while systemMessage worked the whole time
